verdicts.reason: Both score narration of prior involvement in the same docket with the identical exemplar list (prior filings, amendments, pilots, waivers, precedents) and the same zero anchor.
Both require the commenter's own numeric compliance-cost figures with their derivation/basis stated, and both score zero absent numbers.
Both reward a concrete alternative regulatory design specified well enough to implement and score zero when nothing is proposed.
Identical property (a stand-alone emotionally loaded hook line preceding substance); Y only adds an explicit midpoint anchor without shifting either endpoint.
Both contrast developed reasoning/evidence in measured tone against capitalization, repetition, insults, and hyperbole substituting for argument; Y just names the mixed middle.
Both score visible ingest/production artifacts (OCR corruption, duplicated headers, email routing, placeholders, odd spacing) as a surface property against clean prose.
Both score a practicable alternative design that advances the stated objective while addressing the identified defect, with the same zero anchor.
Both require pairing a plausible secondary harm with a concrete safeguard, monitoring step, exception, or contingency, and both zero out bare harm prediction.
Both score firsthand observation aimed at a named factual premise the agency relies on, with the same examples and the same preference-only midpoint.
Both ask whether the instrument would bind at all using the same probes (limit above practice, threshold never triggered, failed voluntary approach, model resolution) and the same anchors.
A developed ultra-vires statutory-authority argument is a distinct property from the presence of part/section CFR citations; a comment can easily have either without the other.
Both score praise of the agency, its staff, effort, priorities, or process while excluding the pro-forma thanks and third-party praise of the policy goal, with the same midpoint.
Emotional intensity of expression and description of first-hand operational practice are unrelated properties; a flat technical operator account scores opposite ways on the two.
Both score verbatim repetition of a sentence or phrase as a surface property with the same 3-or-more top anchor; Y merely omits the explicit exactly-twice midpoint.

Both score adversarial legal-brief posture from the same features (statutory conflict claims, plain-text mandates, legal jeopardy, formal violations, requested remedies); Y adds a midpoint and a correctness disclaimer.
Both require correctly separating mandatory from discretionary elements and reasoning about the difference, versus treating the proposal undifferentiated; Y only names the passing-mention middle.
Both score whether claims rest on locatable, checkable support with relevance and limitations explained, against vague 'studies show' references.
Both score explicit identification and weighing of a genuine tradeoff or counter-consideration while holding one's position, against pure one-sidedness.
Both require concrete explanation of how affected parties would implement, administer, document, or comply plus naming specific operational obstacles, against abstract treatment.
Both score the presence and checkability of a named intermediate-step causal chain from rule to effect, with the same anchors and the same not-agreement caveat.
Both score whether a stated requested change is anchored to an identified paragraph, section, or table, judging the anchoring rather than the merit; Y adds a broad-part midpoint.
Both score density of the same enumerated filing conventions (address block, Re: caption with docket/RIN, membership footnotes, formal salutation, titled signature) as pure formatting.
Both require targeting a specific premise, dataset, model, or inference with concrete evidence or reasoning that could revise it, against mere disagreement with the conclusion.
Both score only the presence of a stated count of members, employees, customers, or constituents, with the same explicit ban on crediting argumentative strength.
Both score foregrounding of quantified membership, customers, assets, market share, reach, or prestige; Y omits the explicit midpoint but tracks the same prominence property.
Both score granular inside-the-operation particulars (workflow, equipment, filing, validation, staffing, transition, compliance process) against broad policy preferences.

Both require locating a particular gap in the agency's notice, preamble, or impact analysis and explaining why it bears on the decision; Y's extra example and record framing do not change the property.
Both score concreteness of the requested change (exact replacement wording, specific numeric threshold, unambiguous procedural modification) against a general for/against stance.
Both require quoting or precisely citing the controlling provision and demonstrating the conflict or omitted required procedure, with the same asserted-tension midpoint and decorative-citation zero.
